source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Physics (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring; stems restated in our own wording, data exact, no solution content by policy. Sections: VSAQ 11, SAQ 5, LAQ 4, PROBLEM 15 numbered problems (22 entries after splitting the (i)/(ii)/(a)/(b) parts of problems 6, 9 and 15). The FORMULAE block on scan pp.71–72 (printed 73–74) is not indexed. The scan crops the outer margins: some question numerals and asterisks are partly cut (LAQ 1, 2, 4; problems 10, 11) and the right edge of problem 7's stem is lost — its data were confirmed from the values used in the printed working.

questions.stem: Give two examples of periodic motion that is not oscillatory.
A girl sits on a swing and is swinging. What is the effect on the frequency of oscillation if she stands up?
The bob of a simple pendulum is a hollow sphere filled with water. How does the period of oscillation change if the water begins to drain out of the hollow sphere?
Will a pendulum clock gain or lose time when it is taken to the top of a mountain?
What happens to the energy of a simple harmonic oscillator if its amplitude is doubled?
Can a simple pendulum be used in an artificial satellite?
Can a simple pendulum oscillate at the centre of the earth? Why?
What happens to the time period of a simple pendulum if its length is doubled?
questions.notes: Printed typo: the book prints 'timer period' for 'time period'.

questions.stem: Write the expression for the total energy of a simple harmonic oscillator.

questions.stem: A particle executes simple harmonic motion such that the maximum velocity during the oscillation is numerically equal to half the maximum acceleration. What is the time period?
A mass of 2 kg attached to a spring of force constant 260 N m⁻¹ makes 100 oscillations. What is the time taken?
A simple pendulum in a stationary lift has time period T. What is the effect on the time period when the lift moves up with uniform velocity?
